What are neutrophils and what do they do?
Neutrophils are a type of white blood cell that helps heal damaged tissues and resolve infections. Neutrophil blood levels increase naturally in response to infections, injuries, and other types
sampled:
of stress.
Neutrophils are the first line of defense against infections, and they help fight off bacteria, fungi, and viruses. Neutrophils work as a team with other immune cells including macrophages and monocytes.
How do neutrophils fight infection?
Neutrophils have long been the target of the scientific efforts to understand the immune response to infection, and are the first cells activated to fight infection.
Like all white blood cells, neutrophils can ingest and digest pathogens in the bloodstream. The ingested pathogens are broken down by the neutrophils, and some of the bacteria and fungi are converted into neutralized byproducts.
Other neutrophils produce reactive oxygen species (ROS) to destroy bacteria and fungi. ROS are produced by a group of proteins called cytochrome oxidase (COX) that are present on the surface of neutrophils. The COX proteins are also present on many other cells in the body.

The first time I saw the data-driven BI market segmentation model from Gartner, I thought it was a waste of time. But then I saw the model and realised it was the only way I could understand the market.
Gartner's market segmentation model is based on the buyer's approach to BI. There are 3 distinct buyer types, and a 4th with a mixed approach. These are:
The core BI user — a small number of people who own the entire BI initiative. The self-service BI user — an even smaller number of people who do not own the entire BI initiative, but who do consume data. The business user — a large number of people who are not core BI users, but who are interested in using BI to make decisions. The data explorer — a large number of people who are interested in using BI to make decisions, but who are not interested in consuming data.
The four groups have different interests, knowledge, and expectations.
